newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil wants U.S. concessions on trade - report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil wants U.S. concessions on trade - report.

text.p: Brazil remains committed to opening its markets to foreign imports but wants reciprocal concessions from the United States, Trade and Industry Minister Francisco Dornelles said in an interview published on Sunday.
"We need to challenge more these barriers which exist against Brazilian exports," Dornelles told the Jornal do Brasil.

A technical study by the Brazilian embassy in Washington said the U.S. was heavily restricting foreign investment and imports of Brazilian goods through a number of trade barriers, the newspaper said.
Sectors affected by the measures included telecommunications, banking, shoes, textiles and the public sector, it quoted the report as saying.
Brazil's share of the U.S. orange juice import market has fallen to 57 percent in 1995 from 90 percent in 1992 as a result of tariffs, the report said.

"Brazil will not make any additional gesture (to open up its economy) unless it is in exchange for measures by other partners," Jose Graca Lima, head of the economic department at the Foreign Trade Ministry, told the Jornal do Brasil.
The remarks followed a speech by President Fernando Henrique Cardoso in London last week in which he urged the European Union to drop barriers to Brazilian products.
Trade has become an increasingly sensitive issue in Brazil, which posted a record $5.5 billion trade deficit in 1996, expected to rise to around $8.0 billion this year.
